feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing responsibility and strong mission-driven relevance.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms and scale indicators (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Writing is polished and strategic, with a strong executive profile and consistent focus on digital transformation, governance, and cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: include growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, campaign results, cost savings, or team/budget size to sharpen impact.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs versions without it); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” for smoother phrasing.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more concise opening, stronger emphasis on recent leadership/modernization work, and less overlap with the competencies sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and mission-driven/public-sector relevance; reduce the long channel list.
- Emphasize recent strengths: digital strategy, CMS/platform modernization, governance, analytics, and cross-functional leadership.
- Tighten the final sentence to show impact: translating complex policy/technical issues into accessible, audience-focused communications.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, digital governance, and the workflows and analytics that support complex teams. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “multi-channel communication” with stronger, CV-aligned phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Consolidate overlapping workflow items into one sharper competency, e.g. “Editorial, workflow & governance systems.”
- Prioritize more senior, recent strengths: digital transformation, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, and advocacy/public-sector communications.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS & web platform administration • Editorial, workflow & governance systems • Data analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and Topline Skills/Technical sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented leadership entry. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact contributions and align it with the project highlights already shown elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by redesigning digital workflows, analytics and governance across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work outcome-based: mention number of microsites, toolkit launches, faster publishing, improved reuse, or engagement gains if available.
- Rephrase technical execution more concisely: “Built and supported Drupal-based public web experiences, including front-end implementation, CMS enhancements and issue resolution.” Add metrics if possible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites and anniversary/campaign work already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail here.
- Governance, analytics and enterprise web improvement overlap with the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new/current in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if channel-management bullets emphasized outcomes, not scope already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channels/results more specific: add growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or campaign outcomes for email/social/video if available.
- Combine operations/analytics into one stronger bullet: “Built enterprise reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the opening and prior NACo role; keep only if you can add measurable results.
- Video leadership may partially overlap with the footer project list; avoid repeating the same studio/program details verbatim.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, with sharper verbs and any measurable outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function at this stage: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow language with specifics if possible: “Built cross-team editorial planning routines and publishing workflows that improved coordination among communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director role; focus this entry on execution/editorial coordination instead of channel oversight.
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; clarify this version as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and audience/governance strengths rather than repeating generic digital strategy language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider “high-volume publishing” or “enterprise governance” to better reflect the 10,000+ page site and 50+ publishers.
- Use “audience-centered” instead of “audience-focused” for a more standard CV phrase.
- If space allows, align wording with recent work by foregrounding governance/editorial systems over broad “content leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or dated items unless central to target roles: remove “jQuery”; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if required by the job.
- Put the strongest, most recent themes first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, add light scope language: “enterprise Drupal platforms” or “large public-facing web properties” to echo recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic, with detailed tools left below.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating it verbatim in both places if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics infrastructure: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework design and executive/leadership reporting
- User behavior, content performance and conversion analysis
- SEO, experimentation and optimization insights
- Put the most strategic items first: KPI design, executive reporting, analytics infrastructure.
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with a sharper outcome-oriented phrase like “SEO, user behavior and content performance optimization.”
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier such as “enterprise analytics reporting” or “cross-channel performance measurement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; use this section for strategic analytics strengths, and keep full tool inventory in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, operational, and tied to recent leadership-level delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual production workflows**
- If space allows, emphasize scope over tasks: **In-house studio buildout, livestream operations and recurring advocacy/event programming**
- Avoid listing basic execution terms if targeting leadership roles; prioritize systems ownership and production oversight over “editing” alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already listed in Core Competencies; consider removing one or making this version more technical.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with work-history references to event/video production, so keep this skills item concise rather than descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating names only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add brief qualifiers only where you have recent, credible depth; this makes the list more senior and aligned to current work.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”
- If space allows elsewhere, add version/scale context for Drupal rather than here (e.g., Drupal 10, 10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Consider removing GitHub Pages if it’s not materially relevant to recent roles; it can make the list feel less enterprise-focused.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent work and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; it feels dated and adds no value.
- If accurate, add a qualifier for impact/level: “for Drupal-based public websites, campaign microsites, analytics tagging and workflow automation” to connect the list to recent consulting and NACo work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary this section to include only tools not named elsewhere.
- “GitHub Actions” and “Cloudflare Workers” are the most distinctive items here; keep those if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used recently or materially in current/recent roles; cut weaker/older items if space is tight.
- If possible, add one proof point elsewhere instead of expanding this list, e.g. “Built Airtable- and Power Automate-based workflows to improve cross-team publishing coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are very common and low-signal unless central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare relative to the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale and relevance to recent email leadership. Make it tighter and more strategic by emphasizing enterprise/member communications tools.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Replace with: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add light qualifiers: Enterprise journeys • Member communications • Newsletter operations
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; keep this item tool-specific.
- Avoid adding outcomes here if they already appear in NACo experience bullets (e.g., newsletter reach); reserve metrics for work experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, site refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution, not generic support: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer action/results language: “Supported a major website refresh, helping modernize the organization’s digital presence and publishing workflows.”
- Tighten multimedia phrasing: “Produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand member-facing communications.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or quantify if possible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/early production rather than expansion.
- “strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; specify this as early process-building to avoid sounding generic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the policy/research language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout contribution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb/outcome, e.g., “produced supporting digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audiences served, or types of projects/campaigns supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item more research/program-focused plus the podcast first.
- Avoid overclaiming leadership in digital operations here, since stronger, more recent leadership appears in 2015–2024 roles.
